problem: Write a JavaScript function Palindrome(str) that returns true if the string str reads the same forwards and backwards, and false otherwise.
notes: Board shows a reverse-and-compare palindrome check. The approach is correct, but line 4 calls .split('') on an array where .join('') was intended, so str2 never becomes a string. Line 5 then compares a string to an array with ===.

preserve_checks.description: Line 4 must stay .split (not be corrected to .join)
Line 5 must stay a direct str===str2 comparison
Line 3 must stay a standalone str2.reverse() call

known_errors.description: str2.split('') is called on an array (TypeError); intended str2.join('') to rebuild the reversed string.

acceptable_findings.description: str===str2 compares a string to an array, so it is always false (consequence of E1).
Edge-case question: case sensitivity, spaces/punctuation, or empty string.
